idiom_name: TypedArray views over one ArrayBuffer (struct of arrays) plus monomorphic object shapes
implementation_notes: The layout comes from the platform's binary views: allocate one ArrayBuffer and create Float32Array/Int32Array views per field (struct of arrays) - a typed array is 'an array-like view of an underlying binary data buffer' with fixed element sizes and no per-element object, which replaces the object-per-entity graph whose traversal hops around the heap. The engine rewards the shape: V8 tracks an elements kind per array (PACKED_SMI_ELEMENTS, PACKED_DOUBLE_ELEMENTS, PACKED_ELEMENTS) and transitions only run from specific to general, so keeping one numeric kind and no holes keeps accesses on the fast path, and monomorphic access sites keep inline caches from going polymorphic. Where objects remain (eventual cold data), give them one stable shape - same properties, same order - and keep the hot numbers in typed arrays.
pitfalls: Elements-kind transitions are one-way: pushing a float (or -0, NaN, Infinity) into an integer array, or creating a hole, downgrades it permanently and slows every later access.
Typed arrays are views: byteOffset/length must be element-aligned and within the buffer, and a detached or out-of-bounds view silently reports length 0.
Reading past an array's length taints the load site in V8 (it falls back to prototype-chain lookups); loops must terminate at length, not at a falsy element.
Garbage-collected objects still dominate if the hot data is a graph of ordinary objects; typed arrays only pay where the data can actually be laid out flat.
